question: Find the remainder, if 19²⁰⁰ is divided by 20.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Using the negative remainder concept:

When 19 is divided by 20, the remainder is −1.

Therefore, when 19²⁰⁰ is divided by 20, the remainder will be (−1)²⁰⁰.

Since 200 is an even power, (−1)²⁰⁰ = 1.

**∴ The correct answer is 1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Expression: 19²⁰⁰ ÷ 20

**Formula Used:**

By the Binomial Remainder Theorem, (x − a)ⁿ ÷ x leaves a remainder of (−a)ⁿ.

**Calculations:**

⇒ The given expression is 19²⁰⁰ ÷ 20.

⇒ We can rewrite the base 19 as (20 − 1).

⇒ So, the expression becomes (20 − 1)²⁰⁰ ÷ 20.

⇒ When expanded using the Binomial Theorem, all terms containing a multiple of 20 will be perfectly divisible by 20.

⇒ The only term left to determine the remainder is the last term: (−1)²⁰⁰.

⇒ Remainder = (−1)²⁰⁰

⇒ Since the exponent 200 is an even number, (−1)²⁰⁰ = 1.

**∴ The correct answer is 1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Binomial Remainder Theorem

When (ax + 1)ⁿ is divided by a, the remainder is always 1. When (ax − 1)ⁿ is divided by a, the remainder is 1 if n is even, and (a − 1) if n is odd.

Negative Remainder Concept

A negative remainder simplifies calculations. For example, 19 ÷ 20 gives a normal remainder of 19, but it can also be taken as −1 (since 19 is 1 less than 20). The final remainder must always be converted back to positive if it ends up negative.

Fermat's Little Theorem

If p is a prime number and a is an integer not divisible by p, then ap−¹ divided by p always leaves a remainder of 1.
